prompt: I run a small dog grooming business called Happy Paws in Austin, TX. My website is happypawsaustin.com but people keep telling me they can't find me on Google. Can you look at why and tell me what to do? Here's what's on my site: a homepage, a services page (baths, haircuts, nail trims, de-shedding), a pricing page, a contact page with my address and phone, and I post to a blog occasionally but not much. I have a Google Business Profile but I don't know if it's set up right.

assertions.name: uses-required-output-format
assertions.text: Response contains all required sections: Executive Summary, Biggest Opportunities, Critical Issues, SEO Analysis, Recommended Actions, Implementation Roadmap.

assertions.name: labels-facts-vs-inference
assertions.text: Response explicitly labels findings as Observed, Inferred, or Recommended rather than presenting guesses as facts.

assertions.name: no-fabricated-metrics
assertions.text: Response does not invent search volumes, rankings, backlinks, or traffic numbers; it flags them as unavailable.

assertions.name: covers-local-seo
assertions.text: Response addresses Google Business Profile, NAP consistency, local intent keywords, and review strategy.

assertions.name: prioritizes-correctly
assertions.text: The top Critical issue is genuinely the most impactful (site unreachable/redirect), not a lower-value cosmetic fix.
